points.t: **Golden honey crusts** round the nose and mouth, or thin-roofed blisters leaving collarette erosions.
*S. aureus* (± *S. pyogenes*) in the epidermis; bullous: toxins split at **desmoglein-1**.
**Eczema herpeticum** mistaken for impetigo; cellulitis; an unwell infant.

cause.lead: Bacteria in the top layer of skin, through a break.
points: Entry via **broken barrier**: eczema, scabies, bites, minor trauma, herpes simplex.
**Non-bullous** (~70%): exudate dries to a honey crust.
**Bullous**: staphylococcal **exfoliative toxins** cleave desmoglein-1 → flaccid blisters (systemically = SSSS).
Spread by contact, towels, scratching (‘kissing lesions’).

visuals.caption: Non-bullous (left): bacteria under a golden crust over a shallow erosion. Bullous (right): toxin splits the upper epidermis into a flaccid, superficial blister.
visuals.alt: Skin sections of non-bullous and bullous impetigo

features.lead: Crust or flaccid blister, often on the face.
points: **Honey-coloured crusts** on a red base: nose, mouth, hands, limbs.
**Bullous**: thin blisters, shallow erosions, collarette scale; axillae, trunk, nappy area.
Mildly itchy or sore; fever and nodes more likely if bullous or extensive.
**Skin of colour**: crusts and redness subtler; rely on history.

visuals.caption: Classic non-bullous impetigo in a child: golden crusts around the nostrils and the corners of the mouth.
visuals.alt: Child's face with perioral and perinasal impetigo crusts

items.name: Skin of colour
items.t: Crusted golden lesions; redness less visible.

points: Recurrent, failed treatment, **MRSA risk**, widespread, outbreak.
Monomorphic **punched-out** erosions on eczema, unwell → **eczema herpeticum**.

cards.name: Eczema herpeticum
cards.clue: Grouped vesicles → punched-out erosions; painful; unwell.

cards.name: Herpes simplex
cards.clue: Grouped vesicles at a recurrent site.

cards.name: Bullous bites
cards.clue: Grouped on exposed sites; tense blisters.

cards.name: Pemphigus foliaceus
cards.clue: Adult, recurrent superficial erosions; no antibiotic response.

points: Wash lesions gently; no shared towels; avoid scratching.
School / nursery: off until crusted and healed, or **48 h after starting antibiotics** (UKHSA).

rx.drug: Fusidic acid (if peroxide unsuitable or fails)
rx.note: Don’t repeat courses: resistance. Mupirocin only for MRSA via local pathway.

points: Topical **or** oral antibiotic for 5 days (shared decision).
Swab; choose by **sensitivities** and local microbiology.
Recurrent: consider nasal carriage and household decolonisation.

limits.t: Only for proven infection on inflamed skin, briefly.
Worse after 2–3 days, spreading redness or fever → review.

items.t: **Infant with bullous impetigo**, or suspected **SSSS** (tender widespread redness, peeling).
Cellulitis, deeper infection, or systemically unwell.
Immunocompromised with widespread disease, or frequent recurrence (carriage, MRSA).

pearls.t: Peroxide 1% first: a real stewardship win.
Fusidic acid: **5 days, then stop**. Don’t repeat.
Treat the trigger (eczema, scabies, lice) or it comes back.

quiz.q: First-line treatment for localised non-bullous impetigo (NG153)?
quiz.a: Hydrogen peroxide 1% cream 2–3 times daily for 5 days.

quiz.q: Bullous or systemically unwell: what antibiotic?
quiz.a: Oral flucloxacillin for 5 days (up to 7); clarithromycin if penicillin-allergic (erythromycin in pregnancy).

quiz.q: What causes the blisters in bullous impetigo?
quiz.a: Staphylococcal exfoliative toxins cleaving desmoglein-1 in the upper epidermis.

quiz.q: When can a child return to school?
quiz.a: When lesions are crusted and healed, or 48 hours after starting antibiotics.
